title: Maximum Product Subarray
statement: A signal-processing pipeline multiplies gain factors together over a stretch of consecutive stages. You are given gains, a non-empty list of integers that may include negatives and zeros. Choose any non-empty run of consecutive stages and return the product of its gains, maximized over all possible runs, as an int. A run of a single stage is allowed, so the answer for [-7] is -7. Note that two negative gains multiply into a positive, so the best run may pass through negatives.
reference_solution:
def max_product_window(gains):
    best = hi = lo = gains[0]
    for x in gains[1:]:
        cands = (x, x * hi, x * lo)
        hi, lo = max(cands), min(cands)
        best = max(best, hi)
    return best
hints: Kadane-style running state works for sums — what breaks when you multiply and hit a negative number?
Carry TWO states per index: the maximum AND the minimum product of a run ending at i. A negative flips them: the smallest (most negative) running product times a negative becomes the largest.

At each element x compute candidates (x, x*prev_max, x*prev_min); the new max is the largest and the new min is the smallest of these. Track the global best of the running max across all indices — do not just return the state at the last index.
